sources.title: Regulation on the visa regime (consolidated through Official Gazette 108/2026)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs published this consolidated regulation on gov.me on 6 August 2026. Its text identifies all Gazette amendments through 108/2026 and sets the nationality, document and duration rules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of states not listed in Articles 1, 1a, 2 and 3 may enter with a valid foreign travel document containing a visa.

sources.title: Montenegro MFA: Kazakhstan visa regime
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: This current country-specific visa-regime page is published by Montenegro's MFA on gov.me and states both Kazakhstan's ordinary baseline and the dated 2026 exception.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of Kazakhstan may, from 1 May to 1 October 2026, stay in Montenegro up to 30 days without a visa.

sources.title: MFA announcement on full alignment with EU visa policy
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: Montenegro's MFA published this 27 July 2026 announcement on gov.me, expressly identifying the future effective date for the last five temporary nationality waivers.
sources.supportingExcerpt: From 1 November 2026, Belarus, China, Russia, Saudi Arabia and Turkey require a visa for entry.

sources.title: Montenegro MFA: visas and visa issuance procedure
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA's current public visa guidance is on gov.me. Its nationality list predates later Gazette amendments, so this source is used only for the issuance method and not for the current country cohorts.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A visa is issued by the foreign-affairs authority through a diplomatic and consular mission.

policies.title: Montenegro: Article 1 named passport issuers visa-free for 90 days
policies.summary: The current consolidated Regulation's Article 1 grants the listed passport issuers up to 90 days visa-free entry, transit and stay with a valid travel document. This list reflects the consolidated text through Gazette 108/2026, rather than the superseded 2025 web list.
conditions: Valid ordinary travel document issued by the competent authority of the named issuer is required; maximum stay is 90 days.
Hong Kong and Macao are included only because Article 1 expressly names valid travel documents issued by those Special Administrative Regions; this does not infer citizenship from a territory code.

Identity-card, refugee/stateless-document, diplomatic/service-document, third-country visa, residence-permit and APEC-card routes are separate conditional rules and are not generalized by this ordinary-passport policy.
Passport validity, purpose, funds, security checks and final border-admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Montenegro: Peruvian ordinary passport visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Article 3 of the current consolidated Regulation allows Peruvian nationals to enter, transit and stay for up to 30 days with a valid travel document under the reciprocal-travel agreement.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid travel document issued by the competent Peruvian authority, under the reciprocal-travel agreement named in Article 3.
This does not extend to diplomatic/service documents, residence, work or other purposes outside the ordinary short-visitor baseline.

policies.title: Montenegro: Belarusian and Russian ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Article 3a preserves a 30-day visa-free ordinary-travel-document route for Belarus and Russia only through 31 October 2026; the MFA announces visa requirement from 1 November 2026.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid travel document issued by the competent authority, pursuant to the reciprocal-travel agreements named in Article 3a.
This time-limited policy must not be used for travel on or after 1 November 2026; the MFA says a visa then becomes required.

policies.title: Montenegro: Saudi and Turkish ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Article 1a allows Saudi Arabian and Turkish nationals a 30-day visa-free ordinary-travel-document route only through 31 October 2026; the MFA announces visa requirement from 1 November 2026.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid travel document issued by the competent authority of Saudi Arabia or Türkiye.
This time-limited policy must not be used for travel on or after 1 November 2026; the MFA says a visa then becomes required.

policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakh ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Montenegro MFA's Kazakhstan-specific page states that the ordinary visa baseline is temporarily waived from 1 May to 1 October 2026 for stays up to 30 days.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid Kazakh travel document only during the official 1 May to 1 October 2026 seasonal period.
The MFA page states the normal Kazakhstan baseline is visa required; recheck the exact end-of-period treatment before travel after 1 October 2026.

policies.title: Montenegro: Article 4 ordinary-passport visa baseline
policies.summary: For every remaining catalog issuer, Article 4 expressly requires a valid foreign travel document containing a visa. Montenegro's published issuance guidance describes consular issuance, so this is not promoted as an eVisa merely because application support may be arranged online or through a service centre.
conditions: Article 4 is an express residual rule, not an inference from omission: a valid foreign travel document containing a Montenegro visa is required.

No eVisa policy is proposed. The MFA guidance describes visa issuance through diplomatic and consular missions; online filing or a VFS application centre would not itself establish electronic issuance.

For China, Article 6 separately preserves, only through 31 October 2026, 30-day visa-free entry for organized tourist groups with paid-arrangement and return proof, or business-passport holders with an invitation. Those condition-bound routes do not convert the ordinary baseline to visa-free.

Articles 7, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 12a contain separate third-country-visa, residence, special-document, refugee/stateless, diplomatic/service and accreditation exceptions; none changes this ordinary nationality baseline.
Passport validity, stated purpose, documentation, security checks, visa approval and final border admission remain separate requirements.

policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakh ordinary passports require a visa after the 2026 seasonal waiver
policies.summary: After the official seasonal waiver ends on 1 October 2026, Kazakhstan returns to Montenegro's explicit Article 4 advance-visa baseline.
conditions: This future-dated policy must not displace the current seasonal visa-free route on or before 1 October 2026.
The MFA's Kazakhstan page identifies visa-required as the normal baseline; the Article 4 rule requires an advance Montenegro visa and does not establish eVisa issuance.

policies.title: Montenegro: four temporary ordinary-passport waivers end on 1 November 2026
policies.summary: The MFA expressly says Belarusian, Russian, Saudi and Turkish nationals require a visa from 1 November 2026, returning these ordinary passports to the Article 4 baseline.
conditions: This future-dated policy must not displace the current 30-day visa-free route through 31 October 2026.

The announcement also names China, whose ordinary-passport baseline is already visa-required; China's temporary organized-group and business-document exceptions remain separately conditioned through 31 October.
The Article 4 advance visa is issued through a diplomatic or consular mission; no current electronic-issuance route is established.

conflicts.explanation: The consolidated Regulation's Article 12b ended Azerbaijan's temporary waiver on 15 January 2026; Article 4 now supplies the explicit visa baseline.
Bahrain is absent from the current Articles 1 and 1a after the 2026 amendments, and Article 4 expressly requires a visa for the residual ordinary-passport cohort.
Qatar is absent from the current Articles 1 and 1a after the 2026 amendments, and Article 4 expressly requires a visa for the residual ordinary-passport cohort.
Vanuatu is not in the current consolidated Article 1; Article 4 expressly requires a visa for nationals outside the named waiver articles.

unresolved.reason: The reviewed travel-document guidance describes a return certificate for nationals abroad but does not directly establish the citizenship/home entry classification. A current primary legal entry provision is still required.
